newsitem.title: UK: CORTECS TO REGISTER MACRITONIN IN EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: CORTECS TO REGISTER MACRITONIN IN EUROPE.

text.p: Anglo-Australian drug company Cortecs International Plc said on Thursday it planned to register Macritonin, an oral version of an anti-bone-wasting drug, in Europe by the end of this month.
Cortecs said analysis of a double-blind European Phase II/III on Macritonin had confirmed initial positive results announced in May.
Macritonin is Cortecs' oral formulation of salmon calcitonin, a treatment for osteoporosis presently given by injection and, in some countries, via nasal spray.
Cortecs' shares surged 14 percent, rising 22.5p to 185 by 0710 GMT.

"Macritonin should be our first major therapeutic product to be registered, following which we would intend to work towards a product launch at the earliest opportunity in the first European countries," Cortecs said in a statement.
It added it had received approaches from a number of potential marketing partners.
Cortecs aimed to begin U.S. clinical trials on Macritonin in the fourth quarter.
The European Phase II/III Macritonin trial was set to continue for two years to measure the effects of the drug on bone mineral density.
That data will be required for the company's U.S. registration programme.
